CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD  AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY  -3-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:7439-DB  MFA No. 202974 of 2023 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 23.03.2023 passed by the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member MACT-XV, Vijayapura in MVC No.1636/2019.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 08.01.2019 at about 8:30 PM near Wadegaon on Sangola-Mangalweda road, when the deceased Vithal was standing on the extreme end of the road, at that time, a TATA Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.MH- 10/AQ-2502 came from hind side in high speed and in the rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased resulting in the accident thereby, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7439-DB HC-KAR 3.
The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
Respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by the impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.26,84,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7439-DB HC-KAR a)
Firstly, accident has occurred due to negligence of the deceased.
There was no zebra crossing.
he was crossing the highway and suddenly entered the main road.
Therefore, the driver of the offending vehicle was not in a position to control his vehicle and dashed to the deceased.
The Tribunal has not considered this aspect of the matter and erred in holding that driver of the offending vehicle alone is negligent in causing the accident.
b) Secondly, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and thus, the insured has violated the policy condition.
The Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on the insurance company.
c) Thirdly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and hence, sought for allowing the appeal.
7. Though respondents are served, they remained unrepresented.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7439-DB HC-KAR 8.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

9. The case of the claimants is that on 08.01.2019 at about 8:30 PM, the deceased Vithal was standing on the extreme end of the road near Wadegaon on Sangola- Mangalweda road, the driver of TATA Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.MH-10/AQ-2502 came from hind side with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result, the deceased suffered grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
10. As per spot mahazar (Ex.P3) and spot sketch (Ex.P4), it is very clear that accident has occurred on the State Highway and there was no zebra crossing near the accident spot.
It is a straight road.

The driver of the offending vehicle could see a person crossing the road, since the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner; he has not made any attempt to slow down the vehicle to avoid the NC: 2025:KHC-K:7439-DB HC-KAR accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal considering the evidence of PW.2, eyewitness to the accident and spot mahazar, spot sketch, FIR and charge sheet has rightly come to the conclusion that driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
Even though the Insurance Company took the contention that driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence, they have failed to prove the same.
In fact, in the chargesheet, there was no evidence relating to driving licence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
The appellant has failed to make out any case.
As such, the appeal is dismissed.
